# A top-level func that writes a top-level var compiles, and the write lands.
#
# bubbletea puts a package var on the Model, and EvalIdent spells a state var
# `m.log` in every scope it is read from. A top-level func emitted free is a
# package-level Go function with no receiver, so the body named an `m` its own
# signature did not declare and `go build` aborted with `undefined: m`.
#
# `viaBump` is the transitive half and is why this is not one classifier
# reading one body: it touches no var itself and reaches one only through the
# call, so left free it would have spelled `m.bump(…)` instead.
#
# This is the CLI's harness rather than a golden because the claim is that the
# generated Go *compiles and runs*; testdata/toplevel_func_reads_state.txtar
# holds the shape it comes out in.

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:test"
import . "sngl:ui"

var log string = ""

func bump(k int) int {
    log = log + "!"
    return k * 2
}

func viaBump(a int) => bump(a) + 1

component main node {
    var out = 0
    var note = ""

    effect(@mount {
        out = viaBump(3)
        note = log
    })

    text(value="{out}{note}")
}

func testTopLevelFuncWritesTopLevelVar(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.out == 7)
    t.assert(c.note == "!")
}

window {
    main
}
